programme: VEZF1 acting as an endothelial-specific transcription factor on EDN1/GSK3B/CITED2, ELF2 (ETS family) driving the angiopoietin-Tie2 vascular-remodeling axis through TEK/TIE1/ANGPT1/ANGPT2, and PPARD controlling angiogenic and lipid-handling genes (ANGPTL4, PTGS2/COX2, PDK4) — together a vascular endothelial remodeling module rather than a tumor- or neuron-intrinsic pathway
role_in_a: In esophageal cancer this module would run the angiogenic switch that lets the tumor recruit new vessels for growth and invasion: VEZF1 has direct evidence of promoting ESCC cell migration, and PPARD variants are linked to tumor grade and to survival on chemotherapy, consistent with a role in the tumor vascular/metabolic microenvironment.
role_in_b: In stroke the same module would govern the cerebrovascular endothelium's response to ischemia-reperfusion and the angiogenic repair that follows infarction: VEZF1 is implicated in an oxygen-glucose-deprivation/reoxygenation model of brain microvascular endothelial injury, PPARD sits in a metabolic-risk pathway relevant to vascular disease, and ELF2's target set (Tie2/angiopoietin genes) is the canonical vascular-stabilization circuit engaged after ischemic injury.
shared_axis: Both a growing tumor and an infarcted brain territory must remodel their local vasculature under hypoxic stress — the tumor to build a supply line, the infarct to reperfuse and repair — and VEZF1/ELF2/PPARD sit at the transcriptional control point for that endothelial remodeling in each tissue. The two diseases would converge on this programme not because they share a disease mechanism but because both are hypoxia-driven states that recruit the same generic endothelial stress-response wiring.
reasoning: VEZF1 and PPARD are each independently placed in esophageal cancer and, separately, in stroke-adjacent models by the retrieved papers, and the module they form with ELF2 is nameable from gene identity alone (endothelial-specific TF plus the Ang-Tie axis plus a PPAR family angiogenic regulator). No retrieved source states that esophageal cancer and stroke share this axis together, and ELF2 has no disease-specific paper support at all — its place in the module rests entirely on its target list — so the cross-disease link is an inference from each disease's separately established biology (tumor angiogenesis; post-ischemic vascular remodeling), not something the record demonstrates directly.
support: PMID 40747711 - shows VEZF1 associated with esophageal cancer cell migration in a visfatin/miR-3613-5p axis; PMID 34146216 - places VEZF1 in an oxygen-glucose-deprivation/reoxygenation model of human brain microvascular endothelial cells relevant to stroke; PMID 32285752 - links PPARD host variants to esophageal cancer patient survival on chemotherapy; PMID 33960436 - identifies PPARD among tumor-grade-associated genes in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma; PMID 25043640 - links PPAR family polymorphisms to survival in upper aerodigestive/lung cancer; PMID 38161971 - weak, tangential support: reports FTO variants raising type 2 diabetes risk in a paper that also scored PPARD, relevant only insofar as it ties PPARD to vascular-metabolic risk rather than to stroke directly. ELF2: none found.
how_to_falsify: In an esophageal cancer xenograft, knock down VEZF1 and ELF2 (individually and together) and measure microvessel density (CD31) and tumor growth; in parallel, generate endothelial-specific Vezf1/Elf2 conditional knockouts and subject them to MCAO (middle cerebral artery occlusion), then measure infarct-border microvascular density and blood-brain-barrier permeability during the reperfusion window. If neither manipulation changes angiogenic output in either tissue, or if VEZF1/ELF2 ChIP-seq in endothelial cells from esophageal tumor and post-stroke brain tissue shows no shared occupancy at ANGPT1/ANGPT2/TIE1/EDN1, the shared vascular-remodeling account is wrong.
caveats: The tissue pairing (blood for stroke, esophagus for the cancer) means any shared 'endothelial' signal is inferred across two different vascular beds, not observed in matched tissue. Of 69 nominal patient-group comparisons only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie them, so the high supported_in fractions (e.g. HOXA11's 57/69, EGR4's 49/69) reflect repeated subdivisions of very few source cohorts and should not be read as 69 independent replications. The exclusion lists filtered out generic blood/immune regulators (MEF2C, EBF1, TAL1, BCL6, IKZF1) and single-cohort outliers (NANOG, HAND2, SOX4), which is consistent with — but does not itself validate — a more tissue-specific vascular story; ELF2's role here rests on its regulon (Tie2/angiopoietin targets) rather than on any retrieved paper, so it is the weakest link in the module and should be treated as the first candidate to drop if experimental follow-up fails.
